The witness runs cmdCheck -> runCheck -> binaryInfo -> registeredToolCount -> tools.RegisterAll -> IngestCommitMsgTool -> [closure] -> atomicfile.Write. `vp check` COUNTS registered tools; it never invokes one. Accepted.

🔴 THE LOAD-BEARING UNDER-DERIVATION, and the one that refutes generating the flag from the derived answer. Derived FALSE because `vp config sync` reaches no funnel primitive ON THE PATH THAT STILL WRITES RAW. HALF OF THE ORIGINAL PROSE IS NOW FALSE and is corrected here: since 28f2a35 the VAULT branch of reconcile.applyUpgrade does reach the funnel — applyUpgradeVault -> storage.LockedUpdate -> atomicfile.Write under a held vaultlock — so the claim that 'the package contains no atomicfile or vaultfs call at all' no longer holds for that branch. What is still RAW: only the HOST-LOCAL branch (upgrade.go:155,159,163 — backup + temp + rename, deliberately, because a host-local config has no committed pre-image and its .bak is the only one it gets), which is deliberately out of scope (ADR-003 itself calls this branch out as living outside the funnel). template_tree.go's scaffold README write — the last vault-file raw write this entry used to name — is fixed: applyScaffold now creates it via vaultfs.Create (lock-disciplined create-if-absent, no O_EXCL window at length zero) and repairs a crash-left zero-length stub via vaultfs.Write under a sha256("") CAS guard, landed by template-tree-raw-vault-writes-bypass-the-lock-funnel. Both Templates prunes remove through vaultfs.Delete, compare-and-set under the path's lock, so neither is raw: the git-vault prune (storage.PruneMirrorsVerified) always did, and the unversioned-vault prune's raw os.Remove was replaced by it in template-provenance-manifest-retires-the-host-local-lock (re-measured then: the entry is still not stale, because of the two raw writes named at that time). The prune's raw .bak emission this entry used to name was deleted by vault-template-override-is-discarded-by-config-sync; the entry was re-measured then and is still not stale. Re-measured again after the scaffold-README fix (`make source-audit`: ok, no new/stale divergence) and the entry STILL did NOT go stale: the derivation still says FALSE for this root, because upgrade.go's host-local branch alone is reached by every `vp config sync` (there is no --prune flag; upgrade is part of every sync) and remains genuinely raw. DECLARED WINS: `vp config sync` writes and removes vault files — the Templates prune, the retired templates.lock removal, and (host-local only) the config upgrade backup — and adopting the derived answer would silently UNGATE it. That is a coverage regression of exactly the kind that sank the original move-the-gate thesis, and ADR-010's Consequence 'No coverage is lost — vp config sync --prune and vp audit vault --accept keep the gate they have today' (the ADR's wording; the flag never existed, the prune is part of every `vp config sync`) is FALSE for a naive derivation on this half (it holds for vp audit vault --accept only because Phase 4 routed vaultaudit.Baseline.Save through atomicfile.Write). FIX DIRECTION: none remains for a vault-file path — upgrade.go's host-local branch is deliberately excluded from the funnel by ADR-003 and is not expected to change, so this entry is expected to stay accepted (not go stale) indefinitely absent a change to that ADR ruling.

🔴 GIT-MEDIATED — derived FALSE correctly, and gated anyway. `vp vault commit` mutates vault HISTORY exclusively through git, and the git channel is exempt from the write funnel BY VERB (a merge is N files in one operation, which no per-path primitive models; recorded on internal/sourceaudit/vault_write_funnel.go and re-ruled 2026-08-20). So it reaches no sink by the funnel's own definition, and a derivation that GENERATED the flag would silently ungate it. DECLARED WINS: git-mediated authorship is still authorship — `git merge` can leave conflict markers in resume.md — and a stale binary must refuse it. This entry, with its two siblings mcp.vp_vault_sync and mcp.vp_vault_tidy, is the reason the derivation pins rather than generates. Accepted, permanently: this one has no fix direction, because nothing here is broken.

🔴 GIT-MEDIATED — see cli.cmdVaultCommit for the full ruling. `vp vault tidy` classifies the working tree and commits capture artifacts through git; it reaches no funnel primitive. Accepted, permanently.

🔴 FALSE POSITIVE FROM A SHARED GENERIC INSTANTIATION — an imprecision of VTA that neither ADR-010 nor the plan task anticipated, both of which worried only about CHA over-approximation. The witness runs CollectWrapStateTool -> [closure] -> wrapstate.Collect -> wrapstate.OldestRootCommit -> slices.Backward[[]string string]$1 -> storage.pruneEmptyDirs$2 -> vaultfs.RemoveNoLock. `slices.Backward` is instantiated ONCE for []string and shared by its two callers in this module — wrapstate/gitprobe.go:418 and storage/kg_migrate.go:541 — so VTA merges the range-over-func yield closures of a git-log reader and a directory pruner into one node. wrapstate.Collect is read-only; it runs git probes and parses files. DECLARED WINS. GENERALISATION WORTH KEEPING: a derived verdict is only as trustworthy as its witness path, which is why the analysis emits one — this divergence is indistinguishable from a real finding without it. Accepted.

HOST-LOCAL, OUTSIDE THE FUNNEL ENTIRELY — derived FALSE, and correctly so: the tool's only write is EnqueueIterationSummaryTool -> summarize.EnqueueIterationSummary -> enqueue(), which writes a job file straight with os.WriteFile/os.MkdirAll against <project_path>/.vibe-palace/summarization-queue/ — never atomicfile.Write, vaultfs.RemoveNoLock/RenameNoLock, or Vault.appendUnderLock. It touches no vault content at all. DECLARED WINS anyway: MutatingToolNames's own doc comment scopes the gate to 'the vault (OR project-root state)', not vault content alone, and this queue file is exactly the project-root/host-local state class vp_stamp_iter and vp_ingest_commit_msg are gated for — it happens to sit even further outside the funnel than either of those (both of which route their own project-root writes through atomicfile.Write and so do not diverge here), because SummaryItem's on-disk shape is queue mechanics a stale binary could still write incompatibly with a newer drain. Fix direction: none expected — like cli.cmdConfigSync's host-local upgrade branch, this is deliberately raw, host-local I/O outside the funnel by design, not an omission.

SPAWNED-PROCESS-MEDIATED — derived FALSE, and structurally unable to be otherwise: the handler itself performs only a read-only filepath.Glob and, when the queue is non-empty, calls detachlaunch.LaunchFunc to exec a DETACHED `vp drain summaries` child process. That child is a separate OS process, not a Go call, so no static call-graph analysis of this binary can see what it does — including that a future real summarize.Summarizer implementation will write to the vault from inside it. This is the same shape as the git-mediated divergences (mcp.vp_vault_sync, mcp.vp_vault_tidy, cli.cmdVaultCommit): the real mutation happens through a channel invisible to per-function reachability. DECLARED WINS: launching a background writer against this project's vault is exactly the kind of side-effecting action a stale binary must be prevented from doing, so it stays gated even though the parent process itself writes nothing. Fix direction: none expected — a spawned subprocess is structurally opaque to this analysis, permanently, the same way git is.

🔴 GIT-MEDIATED — the sharpest instance of the ruling recorded on cli.cmdVaultCommit, because this tool sits on the recovery path. Derived FALSE: there is no funnel sink anywhere in internal/storage's vaultpull.go, vaultsync.go, vaultsyncflow.go or vaulttidy.go (verified by inspection and by this graph), so its vault writes are git's. DECLARED WINS — it commits and pushes vault history and a stale binary must refuse that. Adopting the derived answer would have LOOKED like a bonus, because the MCP-pull lockout ADR-010 records would dissolve on its own; it would have dissolved as a SIDE EFFECT while push and sync quietly lost their gate. The lockout was instead fixed deliberately in 6254549, by making the gate param-aware so action:'pull' passes while push and sync are still refused. Two ways to reach the same symptom, one of which also removes a gate: that is the whole argument for pinning rather than generating. Accepted, permanently.

DELIBERATE TEST SEAM, declared in non-test code because it must be reachable from another package's tests (cmd/vp). It exists because "how many times did this run write THIS FILE" is not answerable anywhere else: a counter placed inside a command's own executor counts writes THROUGH that executor, and the regression that matters (task-board-fields-migration-fails-on-real-vault-data, D1) is a SECOND writer appearing beside the executor, which never passes such a counter. Every task-file write in the tree bottoms out in atomicfile.Write — vaultWriteFunnel exists to keep it that way — so this is the one honest place for a per-file write count. Exercised by cmd/vp's TestBoardFieldsWritesEachFileExactlyOnce, and proven capable of failing: reintroducing the two-write shape makes that test report 2 writes for every archived file. Production never calls it and nothing in atomicfile behaves differently when it is unset. ADR-006 verdict: REPORT + DECLARE — this is production surface added for a test, which is a real cost the plan recorded rather than hid.

TEST-ONLY BY DESIGN, mirroring the shape of SetMigratorExempt (internal/storage/format_gate.go) but not its call pattern: SetMigratorExempt has one production caller (kg_migrate.go), while SetClock's whole purpose (board-reporting-createtime-modtime-fields) is letting test code pin the instant CreateTime/ModTime stamp to, in place of the real time.Now() every normal caller reads through Vault.now(). ADR-006 verdict: DECLARE + ACCEPT — declared here because it is a genuine, permanent test seam, not a real caller waiting to be wired up.

CORRECT AS WRITTEN — not a vault write at all. internal/absorb/writer.go:465-467 rewrites a PROJECT-REPO source file (ps.AbsPath), and passes vaultRoot="" deliberately so no .surface stamp is attempted, keeping fsync + inherit-perm from the private atomicWrite it replaced. The in-tree comment at :464-466 states this. The rule cannot distinguish a deliberate "" from a mistaken one without type information, so this is the false-positive shape the hazard text tells you to baseline WITH THE REASON. Accepted permanently.

DELIBERATELY EXEMPT — a diagnostic must run when the funnel is what is being diagnosed. internal/check/vaultfs.go:141 creates a transient, self-deleting .vp-fs-probe-* at the VAULT ROOT with O_CREATE|O_WRONLY|O_EXCL to test whether the filesystem accepts ':' in a filename (the NTFS/exFAT case). Routing a filesystem-capability probe through the primitive whose correctness it is probing is circular. The same reasoning already keeps the MCP-side vp_check Mutating:false — see the sibling ungated-vault-writer main.cmdCheck entry. Census row 23.

STRUCTURALLY EXEMPT — the lock primitive cannot take the lock. internal/vaultlock/vaultlock.go:99,107 creates <vault>/.vp-locks/<sha>.lock, which IS the advisory-lock file the whole discipline (ADR-003) is built on. Routing it through atomicfile.Write would require acquiring the lock in order to create the lock, and atomicfile does not lock anyway. Census row 20. Exempt with rationale, not deferred work.
